what: The one-value REMUS 100 hull, mass, site, hull loads and propeller (base file), with every added-mass Coriolis term kept, the body lift in both planes as one point force, four effective-angle fins whose lift slope is computed from the fin geometry, and the propeller roll reaction at the estimated scale. Straight-line stable at its cruise speed. A sibling of REMUS 100 (published reference), not an identification of the vehicle.

base.what: every value not listed below: SpheroidAuv (length, diameter = beam, body_mass from one_value.mass, body_center_of_gravity, roll_added_inertia_ratio), Site (latitude from gravity.latitude_rad, water_density), SubmergedRestoring (center_of_buoyancy, neutral), AuvHullLoads (time_constants, damping_ratios, planform_area, parasitic_drag_coefficient, oswald_efficiency, span), Propeller (all its entries but roll_moment_scale); kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m^2/s

hull_frontal_drag_coefficient.source: axial drag coefficient of the hull on its frontal area, Allen et al. (2000), cited second-hand, not read; the same value the published reference part's hull loads carry

coriolis_form.source: every added-mass Coriolis term kept (Fossen 2011, eq. 6.43, p. 120); kept only with the point-force body lift and effective-angle fins with the geometric lift slope, and only with the straight-line stability gate green

current_form.source: still water (the gates run without current)

body_lift_slope_method.source: Prestero 2001, eqs. 4.30-4.32, p. 30 (Hoerner 1965, p. 13-3, not read); l/d = 1.6 / 0.19 = 8.42, inside the stated 6.7-10

body_lift_slope_per_degree.source: Prestero 2001, eq. 4.31, p. 30 (c_y_beta = 0.003, after Hoerner 1965, not read)

pressure_centre_method.source: Prestero 2001, eq. 4.35, p. 31; nose at +L/2 (hull centred on the body origin)

pressure_centre_fraction.source: Prestero 2001, eq. 4.35, p. 31 (0.65 l); Hoerner's range 0.6-0.7 l as Prestero p. 31 gives it -- the gates also run 0.60 and 0.70

hull_drag_form.source: the drag half of the wing block kept, so that only the lift changes against the published reference part; its induced part still uses the wing's vertical-plane lift coefficient (a residual of that form, stated)

roll_damping_form.source: time-constant damping alone (no identified quadratic roll coefficient for this vehicle)

roll_moment_scale.source: scale of the propeller shaft-torque reaction on the hull (Prestero 2001, Sec. 4.6.2, p. 33); calibrated in the generic-models REMUS actuator set to a steady roll of -5.3 deg at 1500 rpm and 1.51 m/s with that plant; carried over here, not re-calibrated for this plant

fin.what: four Fin parts: two rudder fins on the rudder command, two stern-plane fins on the stern-plane command (the vehicle's inputs are the four fin commands in this order, then the shaft speed; a pair receives one command twice)

lift_law.source: the slope from the fin geometry

aspect_ratio_factor.source: Prestero 2001, eq. 4.39, p. 31 (AR_e = 2 b^2 / S_fin: the body acts as a reflection plane)

section_efficiency.source: Prestero 2001, Table 2.2, p. 17 and eq. 4.38, p. 31 (the empirical factor a-bar, after Hoerner 1965 p. 3-2, not read)

lift_slope_computed.value_note: 3.1158 1/rad per fin = [1/(2 pi 0.9) + 1/(pi 2 0.0857^2/0.00665)]^-1; Prestero 2001, Table 2.2, p. 17 prints 3.12 (derived, not declared)

section.source: C_L = a alpha, C_D = C_L alpha (the angle-free form of the published reference model)

servo_dynamics.source: the command is the deflection, saturated

servo_angle_limit.source: the command saturated at the deflection limit

max_deflection.source: the deflection limit of the base set, 20 deg

fin_position.source: the fin post at the tail of the hull centred on the origin
the fin post at the tail of the hull centred on the origin
the fin post at the tail of the hull centred on the origin
the fin post at the tail of the hull centred on the origin

shaft_speed.source: the shaft speed that holds 1.54 m/s straight (Prestero 2001, Table 8.1, p. 60) in the reference model with every published form, found by reference_torpedo_auv.shaft_speed_holding; a test checks that it still does. The part's own straight-running equilibrium at this shaft speed is its cruise state
